content: 1. Econazole topical foam is flammable. Avoid exposure to heat, open flames, and smoking during and immediately after application. 2. The product is contained under pressure. Do not puncture or incinerate the containers. 3. Do not expose the containers to heat or store them at temperatures above 120°F (49°C), even if the containers are empty. 4. Avoid storing the product in direct sunlight. 5. Concomitant use of econazole and warfarin has been shown to enhance the anticoagulant effects of warfarin. 6. Most reported cases involved application of the product under occlusion, in the genital area, or over large body surface areas, which may increase systemic absorption of econazole nitrate. 7. Monitoring of the International Normalized Ratio (INR) and/or prothrombin time is recommended, particularly for patients applying econazole to large body surface areas, the genital area, or under occlusion. 8. Long-term animal studies to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of econazole topical foam have not been conducted. 9. Oral administration of econazole nitrate in rats has been associated with prolonged gestation. 10. Econazole topical foam is classified as Pregnancy Category C. 11. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of econazole topical foam in pregnant women. 12. Use of econazole topical foam during pregnancy should only occur if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. 13. Econazole nitrate has not been shown to be teratogenic when administered orally to mice, rabbits, or rats. 14. Fetotoxic or embryotoxic effects were observed in Segment I oral studies in rats receiving doses 10 to 40 times the human dermal dose. 15. Similar effects were observed in Segment II or Segment III studies in mice, rabbits, and/or rats receiving oral doses 40 to 80 times the human dermal dose. 16. It is unknown whether econazole nitrate is excreted in human breast milk. 17. Since many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when administering econazole nitrate to nursing women. 18. Following oral administration of econazole nitrate to lactating rats, econazole and/or its metabolites were excreted in milk and detected in nursing pups. 19. Of the 173 subjects treated with econazole topical foam, 1% in clinical trials, 2 subjects were aged 12 to 17 years. 20. In a pediatric maximal use trial, econazole topical foam, 1%, was applied once daily to 18 subjects aged 12 to 17 years with interdigital tinea pedis for 28 days. 21. The safety findings in subjects aged 12 to 17 years were similar to those observed in the adult population. 22. Of the 173 subjects treated with econazole topical foam, 1% in adult clinical trials, 6 subjects were aged 65 years or older. 23. No overall differences in safety or effectiveness were observed between these older subjects and younger subjects.
